segments.text: NAME
paru.conf - paru configuration file
SYNOPSIS
$PARU_CONF, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/paru/paru.conf, $HOME/.config/paru/paru.conf, /etc/paru.conf
DESCRIPTION
Paru's config file. Based on the format used by [[p0]](5)

Paru first attempts to read the file at $PARU_CONF. If $PARU_CONF is not set, paru attempts to read from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/paru/paru.conf. If $XDG_CONFIG_HOME is not set, or the file doesn't exist, paru attempts to read from $HOME/.config/paru/paru.conf. If that file doesn't exist, it will read the system config from /etc/paru.conf.

Additionally, the [[p0]][[p1]] directive can be used to copy paste files into[[p2]] [[p3]]the config. This could be used to extend the system config by including it in[[p4]] [[p5]]your user's config and then defining options.[[p6]]
OPTIONS
Options belonging to the [options] section.
Print search results from bottom to top. AUR results will be printed first.
Print search results from top to bottom. Repository results will be printed first.
Use bottom-up ordering in interactive package selection menus and top-down ordering for ordinary search and list output. This is the default.
Assume all targets are from the AUR. Additionally, actions such as sysupgrade will only act on AUR packages.
Note that dependency resolving will still act normally and include repository packages.
Assume all targets are from PKGBUILD repositories. Additionally, actions such as sysupgrade will only act on PKGBUILD repository packages.
Note that dependency resolving will still act normally and include repository and AUR packages.
Assume all targets are from the repositories. Additionally, actions such as sysupgrade will only act on repository packages.
[[p0]]Mode = aur|repo|pkgbuilds[[p1]]
Select what kinds of packages paru should act on. Multiple modes can be selected by separating them with a comma.

Additionally, a, r and p may be used as short hand for aur, repo and pkgbuilds respectively. Short form modes can also be combined without a comma. E.g. [[p0]]Mode = ar[[p1]] or [[p2]]Mode = arp[[p3]].
[[p0]]SudoLoop [= args...][[p1]]
Periodically call sudo in the background to prevent it from timing out during long builds.
Optionally args can be passed to choose how to loop the command. This may be useful for doas where looping is done differently.
Don't resolve checkdepends or run the check function.
Also install debug packages when a package provides them.
During sysupgrade also check AUR development packages for updates. Currently only Git packages are supported.

Devel checking is done using [[p0]]git ls-remote[[p1]]. The newest commit hash is compared against the hash at install time. This allows devel updates to be checked almost instantly and not require the original PKGBUILD to be downloaded.
Like IgnorePkg but for devel upgrades. Packages matching this will not be tried for a devel update but may still be upgraded if the pkgver changes.

Like IgnoreDevel but targets urls in the source=() array of pkgbuilds. This can be useful if a package has a properly working main git source but also has an unversioned secondary source that doesn't effect the pkgver.
Remove untracked files after installation.
Untracked files are removed with the exception of directories. This allows VCS packages to easily pull an update instead of having to reclone the entire repo.
[[p0]]Provides [= all][[p1]]

Look for matching providers when searching for AUR packages. When multiple providers are found a menu will appear prompting you to pick one. This increases dependency resolve time although this should not be noticeable.
By default only targets and missing packages will be searched for providers. Specifying all will enable this for all packages.
Prompt to import unknown PGP keys from the [[p0]] field of each PKGBUILD.

During sysupgrade, paru will first perform a refresh, then show its combined menu of repo and AUR packages that will be upgraded. Then after reviewing the PKGBUILDs, the repo and AUR upgrade will start with no need for manual intervention.
If paru exits for any reason after the refresh without upgrading, it will be the user's responsibility to either resolve the reason paru exited or run a sysupgrade through pacman directly.

When building and installing AUR packages; instead of installing each package after building, queue each package for install. Then once either all packages are built or a package in the build queue is needed as a dependency to build another package, install all the packages in the install queue.
Print new news during sysupgrade.

Use pacman's [[p0]] flag to automatically confirm package conflicts. Paru lists conflicts ahead of time. It is possible that paru does not detect a conflict, causing a package to be removed without the user's confirmation. However, this is very unlikely.
Commit changes to pkgbuilds made during review.
Exit as soon as any AUR packages fail to build.
By default Paru will continue and try to build other AUR packages.
Keep src/ and pkg/ directories after building packages.
[[p0]]Redownload [= all][[p1]]
Always download PKGBUILDs of targets even when a copy is available in cache. If set to all then this applies to all packages, not only targets.
[[p0]]Rebuild [= all, tree][[p1]]

Always build target packages even when a copy is available in cache. If set to all, then all packages are rebuilt, not only targets. If set to tree, the whole dependency tree is rebuilt, including already satisfied dependencies.
[[p0]]RemoveMake [= ask][[p1]]
Remove makedepends after installing packages. If set to ask, a menu will appear during builds allowing an option to be chosen then.
Show a detailed list of updates in a similar format to pacman's VerbosePkgLists option. (See [[p0]] Upgrades can be skipped using numbers, number ranges, or repo names.

[[p0]]: It is not recommended to skip updates from the repositories as this can lead to partial upgrades. This feature is intended to easily skip AUR updates on the fly that may be broken or have a long compile time. Ultimately it is up to the user what upgrades they skip.
[[p0]]AurUrl = URL[[p1]]
Set an alternative AUR URL.
[[p0]]AurRpcUrl = URL[[p1]]
Set an alternative URL for the AUR /rpc endpoint.
[[p0]]CloneDir = /path/to/dir[[p1]]
Directory used to download and run PKGBUILDs.
[[p0]]SortBy = <votes|popularity|name|base|submitted|modified|id|baseid>[[p1]]
Defaults to votes. Sort AUR results according to the options in "Sort by" visible here: https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/
[[p0]]SearchBy = <name|name-desc|maintainer|depends|checkdepends|makedepends|optdepends>[[p1]]
Defaults to name-desc. Search AUR packages according to the options in "Search by" visible here: https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/
[[p0]]Limit = N[[p1]]
Limit the number of packages returned in a search to the given amount. Defaults to 0 (no limit). This applies separately to repo and AUR packages.
[[p0]]CompletionInterval = N[[p1]]
Time in days to refresh the completion cache. Setting this to 0 will cause the cache to be refreshed every time, while setting this to -1 will cause the cache to never be refreshed. Defaults to 7.
[[p0]]PacmanConf = path/to/pacman.conf[[p1]]
The pacman config file to use.
[[p0]]MakepkgConf = path/to/makepkg.conf[[p1]]
The makepkg config file to use.
[[p0]]DevelSuffixes = Suffixes...[[p1]]
Suffixes that paru will use to decide if a package is a devel package. Used when determining if a pkgver bump is used when the [[p0]] option is set.
[[p0]]NoWarn = Packages...[[p1]]
Don't warn when these packages are not in the aur, out of date, or orphaned.
[[p0]]MinimumReleaseAge = Duration[[p1]]

Refuse to install or upgrade AUR packages whose AUR-reported modification time is more recent than this, and hide them from AUR search results. The value is an integer with an optional unit suffix: [[p0]] (seconds), [[p1]] (minutes), [[p2]] (hours), [[p3]] (days) or [[p4]] (weeks). A bare number is interpreted as days. The delay gives users time to review newly published changes before installing them.

The check applies to the whole resolved transaction, including dependencies. If any package is too new, paru aborts and lists the offending packages. Devel ([[p0]] and similar) packages are exempt, as they are tracked by upstream commit rather than AUR publish time. Note this exemption is keyed on the package name suffix (see [[p1]]), so a package merely named with such a suffix is exempt regardless of how it is built. Disabled by default. Pass [[p2]] to override for a single run.

After downloading PKGBUILDs, paru requests current AUR metadata again and aborts if a protected package changed while the transaction was being prepared. This check uses AUR metadata, not Git commit dates. It does not constrain local PKGBUILD edits or changes to sources downloaded by makepkg.
[[p0]]MinimumReleaseAgeExclude = Packages...[[p1]]
Packages exempt from [[p0]]. Accepts glob patterns.
[[p0]]LocalRepo [= Repos...][[p1]]
Use a local repo to build and upgrade AUR packages.
Paru will act on packages in the enabled repos instead of foreign packages. The repo must already be declared in pacman.conf but does not have to already exist on disk.
Optionally a list of repos to use can be passed. By default paru will consider all local repos, building new packages into the first listed repo and upgrading the packages in other enabled repos.

Foreign AUR packages installed outside any configured local repo (e.g. installed before LocalRepo was enabled, or via ad-hoc [[p0]]makepkg [[p1]][[p2]]) are not checked for updates by [[p3]]paru [[p4]][[p5]] while LocalRepo is active. To check them, run [[p6]]paru [[p7]] [[p8]][[p9]], or bring them into the configured repo with:
[[p0]]Chroot [= path/to/chroot][[p1]]
Build packages in a chroot. This requires the LocalRepo option to be enabled. Optionally a directory may be passed to specify where to create the chroot.
[[p0]]Sign [= key][[p1]]
Sign packages with gpg. Optionally indicate which key to sign with.
[[p0]]SignDb [= key][[p1]]
Sign databases with gpg. Optionally indicate which key to sign with.
Normally upon AUR packages getting updated the old versions will be removed from the local repo. This option disables that behavior, keeping the both all versions and only updating the DB.
Skip the review process.
BIN
Options belonging to the [bin] section.
[[p0]]Makepkg = path/to/makepkg[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file.
[[p0]]Pacman = path/to/pacman[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file.
[[p0]]PacmanConf = path/to/pacman-conf[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file.
[[p0]]Git = path/to/git[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file.
[[p0]]Pkgctl = path/to/pkgctl[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file.
[[p0]]Bat = path/to/bat[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file.
[[p0]]Sudo = path/to/sudo[[p1]]
The command to use for [[p0]] calls. This can be a command in [[p1]] or an absolute path to the file. The SudoLoop option is not guaranteed to work with a custom [[p2]] command.
[[p0]]FileManager = path/to/fm[[p1]]
This enables fm review mode, where PKGBUILD review is done using the file manager specified by command.
This allows the PKGBUILDs and related files to be edited. Changes won't persist unless committed.
[[p0]]MFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to makepkg. These flags get passed to every instance where makepkg is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to makepkg.
[[p0]]GitFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to git. These flags get passed to every instance where git is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to git.
[[p0]]GpgFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to gpg. These flags get passed to every instance where gpg is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to gpg.
[[p0]]BatFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to bat. These flags get passed to every instance where bat is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to bat.
[[p0]]SudoFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to sudo. These flags get passed to every instance where sudo is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to sudo.
[[p0]]FileManagerFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to the file manager. These flags get passed to every instance where file manager is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to file manager.
[[p0]]ChrootFlags = Flags...[[p1]]
Passes arguments to makechrootpkg. These flags get passed to every instance where makechrootpkg is called by paru. Arguments are split on whitespace before being passed to makechrootpkg.
[[p0]]RootChrootPkgs = Packages...[[p1]]
Space-separated list of packages to install when creating the root chroot.
Defaults to "base-devel" if not specified.
Unlike [[p0]] (which installs packages temporarily before each build), [[p1]] packages become part of the root chroot and persist across all builds.
This only affects chroot creation. To apply changes to an existing chroot, you must delete and recreate it.
[[p0]]Pager = Command[[p1]]
Command to use for paging
[[p0]]PreBuildCommand = Command[[p1]]
Command will be executed for each package before it is built.

The command will be run via 'sh [[p0]]' and the command's current directory will be set to the directory containing the package's PKGBUILD. If a package is already built then the build will be skipped but this command will still be run for that package.
The variables PKGBASE and VERSION will be set for the command to use.
ENV
Set environment variables.
[[p0]]Key = Value[[p1]]
Sets the environment variable Key to Value.
PKGBUILD REPOSITORY SECTION
PKGBUILD repositories can be defined by adding a [reponame] section, where reponame is the name of the repository you wish to add.
A PKGBUILD repository acts very much like the AUR in terms of package installation and upgrades. Packages in PKGBUILD repositories also take priority over the AUR so may be used to mask packages.
The layout of a PKGBUILD repository is simply a directory that contains PKGBUILDs. Paru will recursively scan a repository for PKGBUILDs, up to 3 levels by default.
Paru will refresh PKGBUILD repositories when it refreshes repository databases. Refreshing just PKGBUILD repositories can be done with [[p0]]paru [[p1]][[p2]].
[[p0]]Url = https://path/to/repo[[p1]]
Git URL to the PKGBUILD repository. File paths may be used to point to git repos on disk.
If [[p0]] is specified alongside [[p1]], the specified path will be treated as a subdirectory of the repository and paru will only search for pkgbuilds in that subdirectory.
[[p0]]Path = /path/to/repo[[p1]]

Can be used as an alternative to [[p0]] to point to a PKGBUILD repository on disk. Unlike using a URL path, changes to this directory are propagated to paru immediately and not on [[p1]]paru [[p2]][[p3]]. There is also no review step for this kind of repository.
[[p0]]Depth = N[[p1]]
The search depth for PKGBUILD scanning.
Skip review for this repository.
Force regeneration of the .SRCINFO file even if it exists on disk. This is useful for repositories that forget to update their .SRCINFO files.
